items.memoText:
VETO MESSAGE - No. 175
 
TO THE ASSEMBLY:
 
I am returning herewith, without my approval, the following bill:
 
Assembly Bill Number 2859-B, entitled:
 
    "AN ACT to amend the workers' compensation law, in relation to phys-
      ical  therapy  care  provided  through  the  workers' compensation
      system"
 
    NOT APPROVED
 
  This bill would amend the Workers' Compensation Law to allow certified
physical therapy assistants to provide direct care under the supervision
of a licensed physical therapist instead of an authorized  physician  or
podiatrist.
 
  Last year, I vetoed the same bill because it would have placed injured
workers  at  greater risk (Veto No. 266 of 2016). This bill suffers from
the same flaw.

  First, the bill offers  fewer  protections  to  workers'  compensation
claimants  being  treated  by  physical  therapist assistants, including
omission of the requirement that the supervising physical  therapist  be
on-site  in all cases and responsible for the physical therapist assist-
ant  services.  Second,  physical  therapist  assistants,  who  are  not
licensed  by  the  State, would be able to treat under the auspices of a
non-physician provider. Yet under current law, licensed physical  thera-
pists  may only provide treatment to an injured worker upon the referral
of, and supervision by, a licensed  physician.  Accordingly,  this  bill
would  provide an unlicensed sub-provider group with a level of autonomy
not afforded to a licensed group of professionals with more training and
expertise. Finally, rather than reducing costs to the  Workers'  Compen-
sation  system,  this  bill would drive additional costs to insurers and
employers by requiring additional care providers to  directly  supervise
physical  therapy  assistants. For these reasons, I am again constrained
to veto this bill.
 
  The bill is disapproved.                    (signed) ANDREW M. CUOMO
 
                               __________
